hook.text: Normal inheritance gives a gene a 50% chance of passing on — a gene drive pushes it to nearly 100%.

buildup.text: CRISPR-based gene drives copy themselves into both chromosomes — ensuring every offspring carries the edit.

discovery.text: A gene drive could spread malaria resistance through mosquito populations — potentially saving 600,000 lives a year.

twist.text: Once released, a gene drive is nearly impossible to recall — it spreads through the entire wild population.

climax.text: Daisy-chain drives limit spread to a few generations — a safety brake for testing without permanent consequences.

punchline.text: Rewrite a species' genome in the wild — power that demands extreme caution.

quiz.question: What makes gene drives different from normal genetic inheritance?
options: Gene drives skip generations and only appear in grandchildren
Gene drives copy themselves to both chromosomes, ensuring nearly 100% inheritance
Gene drives only work in plants, not animals

details.summary: Gene drives are genetic elements that bias their own inheritance to spread through populations faster than normal Mendelian genetics allows. CRISPR-based gene drives can propagate engineered traits through wild populations, potentially modifying or suppressing entire species over generations.
details.whyItMatters: Gene drives could eliminate malaria by suppressing mosquito populations or save endangered species by removing invasive threats.
takeaways: Gene drives spread engineered traits to nearly all offspring, not just 50 percent
CRISPR enables precise gene drives in sexually reproducing organisms
Potential applications include malaria mosquito suppression and invasive species control

faq.question: How does a CRISPR gene drive spread faster than normal inheritance?
faq.answer: A CRISPR gene drive on one chromosome cuts the corresponding site on the partner chromosome, triggering repair that copies the drive to both chromosomes. Every offspring inherits the drive instead of the normal 50 percent. Within a few generations, nearly the entire population carries it.

faq.question: What safeguards exist to prevent gene drives from going wrong?
faq.answer: Daisy chain drives require multiple components to function, losing potency over generations. Temporal gene drives self-limit after a set number of generations. Reversal drives can undo previous modifications. Split drives require multiple genetic components that separate in wild populations.
